content: High-conviction call for lithium carbonate price to rally to Rmb250k/t, and Equities Will React

Lithium and battery materials are out of the woods since 2H25 thanks to strong demand, echoing our last lithium report in early Nov-25 (see note). Considering demand continues gaining conviction ahead, together with on-and-off supply disruption factors, we remain bullish on lithium price and think it could test the level of Rmb250k/t during the year (possibly in Aug-Sep). With recent correction in Chinese lithium equities on concern of demand destruction if price stays high, we move up our preference on lithium names as we believe they will outperform the rest of the battery chain when the price rises. We raise the preference on lithium; our latest pecking order along the value chain is lithium > cathode > battery > electrolyte > separator > battery parts > anode (see here). Top picks are Ganfeng Lithium, CATL-A, Hunan Yuneng, EVE and CALB.

Reiterate our bullish view on lithium ASP during 2026—Even though lithium price retreated after touching Rmb200k/t in last two weeks, we still see possibility that lithium price could test another critical level of Rmb250k/t in the rest of the year, likely during Aug-Sep (traditional peak season of NEV plus another front-loading export window). Major battery makers should welcome new capacity onboard during Aug-Sep at the least to achieve its yearly output target, indicating a relatively material demand increase in that time. Fundamentals remain solid, which should support another round of momentum on the lithium price uplift, in our view.

Lithium names under our coverage — Stronger lithium prices reflect stronger demand, and this will be positive for equities sentiment along the battery chain. We maintain Buy on both Tianqi Lithium and Ganfeng Lithium, considering both lithium names should benefit from the lithium ASP uplift amid robust on-the-ground battery demand, thanks to their cost edge, scale effect, and other competitive factors. Of the two, Tianqi Lithium's share price is catching up QTD due to the undemanding valuation, and we estimate the trade should still open in the near term. However, we prefer Ganfeng Lithium on a longer time horizon, as it is witnessing double tailwinds of increasing equity volume in carbonate (incl Goulamina, Cauchari, PPG, and Mt Marion) and ASP uplift in the upcycle, while Tianqi should have few volume increments in the next 2-3 years.

Lithium and battery materials are out of the woods since 2H25 thanks to strong on-the-ground demand, echoing our last lithium report in early Nov-25 (please refer to China Battery Materials - Returning to a Demand-Driven Landscape). Considering demand continues gaining conviction ahead, together with on-and-off supply disruption factors, we remain bullish on lithium price and think it could test the level of Rmb250k/t during the year (possibly in Aug-Sep). Citi Commodity Team also sees lithium prices staying elevated in the near term amid a tight fundamental backdrop, please refer to Metal Matters - We see lithium prices staying elevated in the near term for details.
Battery production pipeline reaffirms the strong demand month by month

Channel check with ZE Consulting suggests on-the-ground battery production pipeline extends the strong momentum YTD, easing off previous concerns that (1) NEV might be weaker than expected in FY26, and (2) raw materials cost inflation might put downward pressure on ESS demand as its IRR is highly cost sensitive. According to ZE Consulting, 4M25 battery production was up by 41% YoY to 874 GWh, and within that, NEV battery production and ESS battery production was up by 22% YoY and 99% YoY to 567 GWh and 307 GWh respectively.

NEV battery demand turns out to be resilient YTD, mainly attributable to (1) stronger than expected NEV export YTD, and (2) increasing commercial vehicle % of total NEV battery demand which acquires much higher battery size vs passenger vehicles. Monthly battery installation data pack from Real Lithium suggests that 1Q26 China EV battery installation was +18% YoY to ~176 GWh, thanks to the surging commercial vehicles in terms of both volume hike and upsizing battery. The battery installation of commercial vehicles was up by 109% YoY to 39 GWh, taking up 22% of battery installation in 1Q26 (vs 16% in 2025 and 9% in 2024), as more and more specials vehicles have changed from ICE to BEV.

On-and-off supply disruption on the course of the year

Even though demand has been gaining conviction YTD, lithium becomes more volatile in trading as there are on and off supply disruptions during the course of the year, putting upside/downside risks on the dynamics. Here we list out the topical supply disruption factors and our read on the latest update.

- JXW (-ve to lithium price) - JXW has been suspended since Aug-25 due to the mining permit expiration, the inappropriate mining license as ceramic clay and environmental issues (i.e., river encroachment, tailings treatment, etc.). According to our channel checks with industry contacts & public government announcement, CATL has obtained proper mining permit in early-26 and is still pending approval for environmental license. It's difficult to arrive at a market consensus view on the clear resumption timeline as it depends on the government process instead of the corporate initiatives. Overall, it's a hovering negative alert to the lithium price before the finalized approval.

Lepidolite mines update (+ve to lithium price) – 4 of the remaining lepidolite mine might need to go through the same procedure (i.e., mining permit, environmental license, etc.) sooner or later during the year, indicating further downside risk to the lithium supply. According to our channel check with industry contacts, companies are expediting the lepidolite production YTD to pile up the lepidolite inventory for conversion later. That said, if the remaining lepidolite mines do need to suspend for a license update, the actual impact this year might be less than the on-paper figures (-8k tons LCE per month, taking up 7-8% lithium supply in China), but the impact in FY27 or years after depends on the approval timeline.

Australian mines update (-ve to lithium price) – Australian high-cost spodumene mines are gradually incentivized to restart and/or expand since 2H26 due to the attractive spodumene prices YTD. Below please find the summary on incremental spodumene incentivized from high spodumene price.

Zimbabwe (+ve to lithium price) – Zimbabwe resumes the spodumene export by end of Apr-26, after its ~3 months spodumene export restriction since Feb-26. We estimate the shipment should gradually arrive in China by end June / early July, easing off the tight spot market dynamics. On top of that, companies will be charged a 10% export rate out of revenue when exporting the spodumene in Zimbabwe, indicating cost inflation on spodumene/lithium conversion ahead.

Investment thesis —Ganfeng Lithium should benefit from the lithium ASP uplift amid robust on-the-ground battery demand and improving cost competitiveness on increasing contribution from low-cost upstream resources (i.e., Goulamina, Mariana, and others). Its continual improvement in equity-owned lithium volume in the next 2-3 years (incl. Goulamina, PPG, Cauchari, and others) laid solid foundation on its long-term competitiveness. Also, its fast-developing battery business should provide further upside support to the headline NP in the upcoming years.

Model update — We update our Ganfeng Lithium financial model post FY25 & 1Q26 results set to factor in (1) the strong start of the year on back of soaring lithium ASP in 1Q26, (2) re-built lithium segment driven by integrated part with equity volume and non-integrated part on pure conversion business, and (3) trending better battery business which could largely pass through the raw materials cost inflation (incl. lithium, copper, ali, etc.). We revise up our FY26/27 headline net profit to Rmb8,457 mn and Rmb8,161 mn with blended VAT-included lithium carbonate and spodumene ASP assumption at Rmb175k/t and US$2,300/t in FY26 and Rmb160k/t and US$2,050/t in FY27 respectively. Introduce FY28 estimates.

Valuation — Reiterate our Buy rating on Ganfeng Lithium-A, and our new TP is set at Rmb93/sh, based on 3.2x 2026E P/B, at the historical 5-year average level since 2021, factoring in the tight S/D lithium dynamics ahead. Implied 2026E P/E is ~22x. Ganfeng Lithium-A currently trades at 2.6x 2026E P/B and 17.3x 2026E P/E respectively.

Jiangxi Ganfeng is one of the largest lithium producers in China. Established in 1996, the company went public in the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2010 and in the HKEx in 2018. With most of its operations in Jiangxi province, the company has ~116kt lithium carbonate and ~131kt lithium hydroxide capacity as of YE2025.

We rate Ganfeng Lithium as Buy. The company should benefit from the lithium ASP uplift amid robust on-the-ground battery demand, and improving cost competitiveness on increasing contribution from low-cost upstream resources (i.e. Goulamina, Mariana, and others). Its continual improvement in equity-owned lithium volume in the next 2-3 years (incl. Goulamina, PPG, Cauchari, and others) laid solid foundation for its long-term competitiveness. Also, its fast-developing battery business should provide further upside support to the headline NP in the upcoming years.

TP is set at Rmb93/sh for Ganfeng Lithium-A based on 3.2x 2026E P/B, at the 5-year historical average level since 2021, factoring in the tight S/D lithium dynamics set-up ahead. Implied 2026 P/E is 22x.

Key downside risks that could impede Ganfeng Lithium A-share from reaching our target price include: (1) geopolitical risk on its overseas mining assets, (2) lower-than-expected lithium-ion battery demand, and (3) slower-than-expected ramp-up of Goulamina and Mariana.

We value Ganfeng-H at HK$78.12/share, set at a 30% discount to our Ganfeng-A target price and after factoring in the exchange rate. The 30% discount is in line with the historical average H/A-share discount since 2020.

Key downside risks that could impede Ganfeng Lithium H-share from reaching our target price include: (1) geopolitical risk on its overseas mining assets, (2) lower-than-expected lithium-ion battery demand, and (3) slower-than-expected ramp-up of Goulamina and Mariana.

As of YE2024, Tianqi Lithium had 1.62mntpa spodumene capacity and 91,800tpa lithium compound capacity. Tianqi has a 26.01% stake in Talison, which controls the Greenbushes spodumene (lithium ore) mine in Australia, the largest spodumene mine in the world with the highest grade of lithium ore (Li2O at 1.3%). This move has enabled Tianqi to secure low-cost mineral resources. Tianqi's products, including lithium carbonate and lithium hydroxide, are widely used in electric vehicle batteries, industrial grease, ceramics, and glass.

We rate Tianqi Lithium as Buy. The stock is one of the best positions to benefit from lithium upcycle, on back of its pure exposure to lithium space from upstream spodumene to downstream lithium carbonate. Lithium price uptick supports Tianqi with decent earnings recovery in 1Q26, and suggests solid financial performance on the course of the year. Also, Tianqi Lithium's undemanding valuation vs Ganfeng Lithium indicates attractiveness to investors in the near term.

We use a P/B multiple for better apple-to-apple comparison vs Ganfeng Lithium. Our TP is set at Rmb75.14/sh based on 2.5x 2026E P/B, the historical average level since 2021 to reflect the tight S/D lithium market dynamics ahead.

Key downside risks that could impede Tianqi Lithium A-share from reaching our target price include: (1) weaker-than-expected lithium-ion battery demand, and (2) any supply disruption on the policy uncertainties.

Guide to Citi Fundamental Research Investment Ratings:
Citi stock recommendations include an investment rating and an optional risk rating to highlight high risk stocks.
Risk rating takes into account both price volatility and fundamental criteria. Stocks will either have no risk rating or a High risk rating assigned.

Investment Ratings: Citi investment ratings are Buy, Neutral and Sell. Our ratings are a function of analyst expectations of expected total return ("ETR") and risk. ETR is the sum of the forecast price appreciation (or depreciation) plus the dividend yield for a stock within the next 12 months. The target price is based on a 12 month time horizon. The Investment rating definitions are: Buy (1) ETR of 15% or more or 25% or more for High risk stocks; and Sell (3) for negative ETR. Any covered stock not assigned a Buy or a Sell is a Neutral (2). For stocks rated Neutral (2), if an analyst believes that there are insufficient valuation drivers and/or investment catalysts to derive a positive or negative investment view, they may elect with the approval of Citi management not to assign a target price and, thus, not derive an ETR. Citi may suspend its rating and target price and assign "Rating Suspended" status for regulatory and/or internal policy reasons. Citi may also suspend its rating and target price and assign "Under Review" status for other exceptional circumstances (e.g. lack of information critical to the analyst's thesis, trading suspension) affecting the company and/or trading in the company's securities. In both such situations, the rating and target price will show as “—” and “-” respectively in the rating history price chart. Prior to 11 April 2022 Citi assigned "Under Review" status to both situations and prior to 11 Nov 2020 only in exceptional circumstances. As soon as practically possible, the analyst will publish a note re-establishing a rating and investment thesis. Investment ratings are determined by the ranges described above at the time of initiation of coverage, a change in investment and/or risk rating, or a change in target price (subject to limited management discretion). At times, the expected total returns may fall outside of these ranges because of market price movements and/or other short-term volatility or trading patterns. Such interim deviations will be permitted but will become subject to review by Research Management.
Your decision to buy or sell a security should be based upon your personal investment objectives and should be made only after evaluating the stock's expected performance and risk.
Catalyst Watch/Short Term Views ("STV") Ratings Disclosure:

Catalyst Watch and STV Upside/Downside calls: Citi may also include a Catalyst Watch or STV Upside or Downside call to indicate the analyst expects the share price to rise (fall) in absolute terms over a specified period of 30 or 90 days in reaction to one or more specific near-term catalysts or events impacting the company or the market. A Catalyst Watch will be published when Analyst confidence is high that an impact to share price will occur; it will be a STV when confidence level is moderate. A Catalyst Watch or STV Upside/Downside call will automatically expire at the end of the specified 30/90 day period. The Catalyst Watch will also be automatically removed if share price performance (calculated at market close) exceeds 15% against the direction of the call (unless over-ridden by the analyst). The analyst may also remove a Catalyst Watch or STV call prior to the end of the specified period in a published research note. A Catalyst Watch/STV Upside or Downside call may be different from and does not affect a stock's fundamental equity rating, which reflects a longer-term total absolute return expectation. For purposes of FINRA ratings-distribution-disclosure rules, a Catalyst Watch/STV Upside call corresponds to a buy recommendation and a Catalyst Watch/STV Downside call corresponds to a sell recommendation. Any stock not assigned to a Catalyst Watch Upside, Catalyst Watch Downside, STV Upside, or STV Downside call is considered Catalyst Watch/STV No View. For purposes of FINRA ratings distribution-disclosure rules, we correspond Catalyst Watch/STV No View to Hold in our ratings distribution table for our Catalyst Watch/STV Upside/Downside rating system. However, we reiterate that we do not consider No View to be a recommendation. For all Catalyst Watch/STV Upside/Downside calls, risk exists that the catalyst(s) and associated share-price movement will not materialize as expected.
